May, 2023
Author: Navneet Kumar

Bench: Navneet Kumar
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
 Cr. Appeal (Sj) No. 27 of 2023
 1.Bablu Rana @ Vinay Kumar

 3.Tinku Sahu @ Vikash Kumar Sahu
 4.Sunil Rana @ Sunil Kumar Sharma

5.Pankaj Rana @ Pankaj Kumar Rana
 6.Jivlal Rana --- --- Appellants

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Navneet Kumar For the Appellants : Mr. Sudhir Kumar Roy,
Advocate For the State : Mr. Vishwanath Roy, Spl.P.P. For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. Shambhu Nath
Tiwari, Advocate 05/19.05.2023

Heard learned counsel for the appellant and the learned A.P.P.
assisted by learned counsel for the respondent no.2.
2.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellants that the instant criminal appeal has been preferred against the order dated 17.12.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge SC/ST, Giridih whereby the anticipatory bail application of the appellants has been rejected in A.B.P. No. 2033 of 2022 in connection with S.C./S.T. Complaint Case No. 13 of 2018.

3. It is submitted on behalf of the appellants that the gist of allegations as set out in the complaint case instituted by the respondent no. 2 was that the complainant/ respondent no.2 while going on motorcycle along with his friend Prakash Rajak on the date of occurrence i.e., 10.03.2018, the complainant was intercepted by these appellants and thereafter it has been alleged that they hurled abusive language upon the complainant/ respondent no.2 by making offensive remark by taking name of his caste and further also snatched sum of Rs.6000/- and also threatened him not to open the school in the village.
It has been pointed out that the complainant and the appellants are on inimical terms and a number of litigations have been between both the parties.

It has also been pointed out by the learned counsel for the appellants that on earlier occasion one victim of the village had instituted a case against the complainant for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC and Section 7,8 and 10 of the POCSO Act in which the appellant no.1 was one of the witnesses and further one case was also instituted by the wife of the complainant namely Meena Devi against these appellants for the offence punishable under Section 147,148,149,341,342,379,323 and 325 of the IPC, which is at annexure - 4 of this petition and therefore, it is submitted that these Bablu Rana @ Vinay Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193763984/
1 appellants have been falsely implicated in this case without any specific allegation and all the allegations are omnibus and general in nature.

sentences.text:
It has further been pointed out that in the S/A of the complainant- Respondent no.2 during the court query, it was admitted by the respondent no.2 that there had been previous enmity between the parties and therefore it is urged on behalf of the appellants that no prima facie case is made out under the Section of SC/ ST Act and as such, these appellants deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4.

Learned A.P.P. appearing on behalf of the State assisted by learned counsel for the respondent no.2 has opposed the contentions raised by the appellants and submitted that all the appellants collectively abused and assaulted the complainant and used abusive languages by taking the name of his caste and therefore, they do not deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail, although they did not deny the fact that the appellants and the respondent no.2 are in inimical terms for a long period of time.
5.
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the record of the case.
6. It is the admitted case of the complainant- respondent no.2 that both parties are on inimical terms.

It is also admitted fact that both parties had been in litigating terms and complainant was also an accused for committing offence under Section 376 IPC with the co-villager, which is at Annexure-3 where one of the appellants was a witness and the counter case was also instituted by the wife of the complainant, which is at Annexure-4.

Further, it is found from the S/A of the complainant that no specific allegation has been attributed against any one of the appellant or using the offensive remark by taking name of the caste of the complainant.

The entire allegation are omnibus and general in nature and therefore, in the facts and circumstances, no prima facie case has been substantiated by the complainant for the offence under the SC/ST Act and

hence in the light of the rulings of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hitesh Verma Vrs. State of Jharkhand & another reported in (2020) 10 SCC 710, the appellants deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
7.

entities.text: Hitesh Verma Vrs. State of Jharkhand & another reported in (2020) 10 SCC 710
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appellants, named above, are directed to surrender within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order, in the court below and the learned Court below is directed to enlarge the appellants in the event of their arrest or/ surrender on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of Learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Giridih in connection with S.C./S.T.
Complaint Case No. 13 of 2018, subject to the condition as set out under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C. and further condition that appellants will cooperate in the criminal proceeding in the court below failing which, the learned court below shall take appropriate steps for cancellation of bail of these appellants.
8. Instant criminal appeal is allowed.
(Navneet Kumar, J.) A.Mohanty Bablu Rana @ Vinay Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193763984/
